prompt.text:
Continue from the still. the Explorer in an ivory industrial helmet with an opaque black full-face visor and cyan side-light rings, orange technical coveralls, chest instrument and grey boots stands inside a doming shaped loaf as bubbles re-inflate for the second rise, warm quiet light. Photoreal cinematic scientific visualization, warm polished home realism, ivory-and-orange equipment palette, cyan accent light. Low motion.

At the opening of the shot, Bubbles re-inflate slowly. Ambient (slow, subtle): the dome swells and the cloth shadow moves.

Then, The camera stays wide on the re-inflating bubbles of the doming loaf while the single Explorer stays planted at the left edge, feet still, head raised toward camera, and says over helmet radio in a calm adult male English voice: "The workers are at it again, slower now." His mouth returns to rest.

Then, The Explorer holds still, head tilted, while Control answers in a calm adult English voice: "Warmth sets their pace; a cool corner would slow them further. Given time, the shaped loaf fills with gas again. This patience is where much of the flavour quietly builds." The Explorer stays in place, mouth closed.

Finally, The camera holds wide with a slight drift across the re-inflating bubbles. The camera ends on the re-inflating bubbles and the slowly doming loaf surface, with the single Explorer still small at the left edge. Acoustic environment: soft returning bubbling; clear close dialogue front and center. The Explorer stays in place at the left edge, mouth closed.

Reference lock: continue directly from the supplied still/reference image; it is the authoritative first frame and starting composition. Preserve the exact character identities, character count, wardrobes, set layout, lighting, and every visible prop's physical size, shape, placement, and attachment. Animate only the character actions explicitly requested in the scene direction. Keep all unattended characters, props, and background elements stationary within the scene. Follow the camera movement explicitly requested in the scene direction; if none is requested, keep the camera locked to the reference framing. Directed camera motion may change framing, perspective, screen positions, apparent size, and visibility without physically moving or changing the scene's objects. Do not introduce, duplicate, physically remove, relocate, reshape, or float any character or prop.
